title: Hive
intro: A new ground above the city.
summary: A capstone proposal at 2301 NW 33rd Avenue, Miami, connecting a neighborhood edge, residences, and a canal-side public realm.
sections: The neighborhood and the waterfront

Hive organizes its proposal around three spatial phases: the neighborhood edge, the waterfront, and the connector. The model lets these parts be read together or isolated to understand their relationships.
An elevated shared landscape
Above the office areas, the amenity deck links the residential buildings. Pavilions punctuate this rooftop landscape. In the sea-level-rise studies, the elevated deck is explored as a future ground.
Drawing and inhabiting

Floor plans and paired render views connect the building’s organization to its spatial experience. Open the model to compare levels, inspect the amenity pavilions, and move between the overall composition and an eye-level view.

title: Phalanstery
summary: A bounded urban composition of towers, courts, water, and an elliptical building, linked by a circular route.
credit: Design: Jaime Correa · Revit modeling and architectural views: Brandon A. Hernandez
sections: A collective composition
The continuous perimeter establishes a shared enclosure. Within it, a dense cluster of towers contrasts with the elliptical volume and the isolated tower across the water.
Color as orientation
Cream surfaces, blue volumes, red towers, and turquoise water distinguish the parts of the composition. Repeated window openings establish a rhythm at the scale of the facade.
From axonometric to street

The original architectural views move between the whole arrangement and framed encounters within it. The interactive study extends that sequence through orbit views and walking, with moving figures and gondolas providing a sense of scale.

title: Tranquil River
intro: A hidden spring. A timber ribcage.
summary: Tranquil Oasis explores a sequence of shelter and openness along the turquoise waters of Kikuletwa Hot Springs.
credit: Brandon A. Hernandez · Design portfolio study
sections: A sequence along the water
The proposal follows a progression through gates, connecting tunnels, and public and intimate sanctuary spaces. Compression and release shape the experience of moving beside the spring.
Repetition and shelter

Repeated timber ribs give the sanctuary its architectural language. The source study describes African Mahogany and Teak ribbing, concrete piers, and a thatch crown. These elements frame water, light, and views.
An atmosphere to explore

The interactive model offers orbit and first-person views, material studies, water controls, and day-to-night atmosphere. Follow the route through the sanctuary or return to a broad perspective to understand how its spaces connect.

title: Net Zero School
tag: Henry S. West Laboratory School · Coral Gables
summary: A K–12 school proposal with separate learning buildings connected by paths, ramps, and shared courtyards.
credit: Design: Brandon Hernandez & Danny Ferrer · Net-zero school proposal
sections: A familiar place, reconsidered
The proposal is for Henry S. West Laboratory School in Coral Gables, Florida—the school Brandon attended as a child. It studies the campus as a collection of connected learning environments.
Program and movement

Distinct program colors help explain the relationship between buildings. Shared paths, courtyards, and ramps connect the ground and upper levels, supporting a reading of the school as a continuous spatial network.
A design ambition

Net-zero is the proposal’s design ambition, rather than a claim of measured performance. The interactive study makes the building arrangement and circulation available for exploration; its real-time materials are interpretations of the supplied geometry and references.
